prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the refrigerator and nearby cabinetry in the first three frames roughly 0.5–1.5 m in front of the camera wearer, while the counters, stove, and back wall are farther away at about 2–4 m; the bright vertical bands near frame boundaries and around the refrigerator suggest close surfaces but are likely depth artifacts. Across the five frames, the view turns right from the refrigerator toward the central kitchen and serving counter, so the refrigerator moves out to the left while the stove and counter move toward the center. In the last two frames, a person appears on the right beyond the counter, roughly 1.5–3 m from the wearer, with the counter between them; the person is approximately 1–2 m behind the cups, bowl, and near counter edge. The map makes near-versus-far surfaces and the counter’s separation from the back wall clearer than RGB alone, but it is unreliable along frame seams, reflective or bright windows, thin objects, dark recesses, and the person’s outline, and it does not reliably reveal facing direction.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies large refrigerator regions in the first three frames, ovens near the center and right-center, a distant person in the fourth frame, and a larger person plus cups, bowls, and a potted plant on the right in the fifth frame. These masks show that the camera turns right across time: refrigerator instances leave the view to the left, the oven shifts across the middle, and the person and tabletop objects enter from the right; the last person is roughly 1.5–3 m from the wearer and stands behind objects that are nearer, around 0.5–1.5 m away. In the final frame, the person is right of the oven, above and behind the bowls and cups, and partly cut off by the right image boundary; the earlier person mask is smaller, consistent with greater distance or partial visibility, and the two person depictions are separated by roughly a few metres in image-derived scene scale if treated as distinct locations. The map makes object identity, overlap, partial visibility, and left/right ordering clearer than RGB alone, but the refrigerator masks are grossly oversized or duplicated, one large region is mislabeled or merged, several cabinets and counter surfaces are missing, and mask labels alone cannot establish gaze or precise metric distance.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects no usable body or hand skeleton in the first four frames and shows only a partial yellow upper-body/arm configuration at the far right of the fifth frame, corresponding to the person beside the counter. The detected person is roughly 1.5–3 m from the camera wearer, to the wearer’s right and behind the nearer counter objects; their visible upper body is partly out of frame, and the skeleton suggests a side-on or oblique orientation rather than a clearly frontal pose, but head and eye direction are too incomplete to determine whether they look toward the wearer. The person’s arms and hands appear close to their own torso and the counter area, while the counter and its bowls or cups are within that person’s probable arm’s reach but not clearly within the camera wearer’s reach. The map can expose limb geometry that is difficult to isolate in RGB, yet here it is highly unreliable because almost all joints and all earlier poses are missing, the detected links do not cleanly match the visible body, and it provides no dependable evidence of approach, retreat, or turning beyond the person entering the right side as the camera view rotates.
